clue.text: Clue 1: house staff refurbished toilet facilities

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done up and rearranged, so the letters before it are reworked

parts.note: taken as written into the pool of letters
one is I as a Roman numeral
taken as written into the pool of letters
taken as written into the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A crossword's first clue about domestic staff giving the lavatories a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clue 1:' looks like a label for the clue but is part of the fodder: CLUE plus I joins HOUSE STAFF, and 'refurbished' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, euphemistic British phrase for the lavatory, so it matches toilet facilities as an idiom.

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening letters of the two pieces are exchanged

parts.note: a poodle is a servile follower, a lackey
a tip is a hint or piece of advice

explanation.surface: A servant's farewell, offered as advice to the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British way of saying goodbye, the sort of thing said when announcing a departure.

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A call for reform now that a political group has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, and 'change' acts only on 'Need'.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to finish there, a phrasal idiom for finally arriving.

indicators.note: worked as in kneaded or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the name Sid

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A quote from referees boasting they collaborated with a man called Sid at a darts match.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'darts' looks like a description but is fodder: WE + S + DARTS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: People who supervise races, events or venues are officials, such as at a racecourse.

clue.text: Master taking time over degree was 6

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the next
the expert takes in time, holding it inside

parts.note: an ace is a master or expert

explanation.surface: An expert takes a while longer to complete a qualification and was something.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' means the answer to 6 down, FAKING, so 'was 6' is 'was faking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a pretence or perform a role is to act, so pretending in the past matches.

parts.note: OK means all right, correct

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A politician has the correct view after a royal overturns a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is wordplay on a resident of a US state, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a US state can playfully be called a statesman; this one comes from the Sooner State.

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: fag is British slang for a tiresome chore
kin are family members

explanation.surface: Making a meal is a drudge, and the relatives were let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' is not culinary but as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook figures is to falsify them, so cooking can mean pretending or forging.

clue.text: Pot hidden in this way after short search

indicators.note: after says the piece for way follows the piece for search
short says the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
a mode is a way or method

explanation.surface: Cannabis was concealed in a certain manner following a brief police search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' tempts as drugs; it is a chamber pot, hidden inside a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture concealing a chamber pot, so a pot is literally kept inside it.

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of the word school

parts.note: vain as in futile, idle threats

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a conceited headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To move furtively sideways is to creep, as both verbs describe stealthy movement.

clue.text: Bit strange having soldiers on square

parts.note: strange means odd
soldiers are men, the ranks
a T-square is the drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Something peculiar about troops drilling on a parade square.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover piece or fragment is a bit, especially a remnant of cloth or a stray item.

clue.text: Furiously rejected female killer? Not half!

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a dame is a woman, a female

indicators.note: not half says only the first half of the word killer is kept

parts.note: the word is taken as written before being cut in half

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a woman who murders, rejected by someone, with the British 'Not half!' meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', which disguises the halving; 'rejected' turns round the whole combined string, giving LIKEMAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something with great energy or speed, the adverb sense of furiously.

indicators.note: away says a piece is taken out of the word for give

parts.note: to give someone something temporarily is to lend

explanation.surface: Asking whether a chaperone revealed someone's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of guiding or accompanying someone, so it fits did escort as a verb in the same tense.

clue.text: Foolish! The names Don gets a lot more than this

indicators.note: foolish suggests silly or deranged, so the following words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram
taken as written into the anagram
taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about someone called Don who receives far more than mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' is a link here; the fodder is THE NAMES DON, eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is tacked on to say there is plenty more besides what was stated, an idiom for even more.

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something unbelievable or wild, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram
taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A gym-goer's remark that two people are equally muscular, followed by fantasies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripped' looks like slang for muscular; it is just fodder alongside SAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrealistic hopes or daydreams that will never come true are a kind of fantasy.

clue.text: Australian natives and another wasting money — flaming typical

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the word for money is lost from the other native

parts.note: another Australian native, the large flightless emu

indicators.note: flaming suggests something burnt up or wild, so the letters are tossed about

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: Grumbling that Australians and a spendthrift are, annoyingly, all too predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another Australian native, EMU, which loses M to give EU; 'flaming' then rearranges TYPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees are native to Australia, and this is the Latin plural of their name.

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for dark is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness

explanation.surface: Someone collected a black car, in short.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal name for a Mercedes car, hence a vehicle given briefly.

clue.text: Jail director with flat in US city

indicators.note: the flat is placed in the jail and director

parts.note: can is slang for prison
level means flat, even

explanation.surface: A prison governor with an apartment inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as an apartment but means LEVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a large city in Ohio, so it is an example of an American urban centre.

parts.note: the cast is the troupe of actors in a production
a rate is a level of pay, a grade on the scale

explanation.surface: A reduction in performers' salary scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a pay reduction but is a verb meaning to geld.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate an animal is to neuter it by cutting, so cut serves as a blunt synonym.

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stroll home from the seat of the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' points to letters taken out of 'the Capitol': ECAP, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A step or a gait is a pace, and to pace is to walk steadily.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for Henry is removed

parts.note: to back a cause is to champion it, a champion being a supporter
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A plant supporting someone other than a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' is H, the symbol for the SI unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering wildflower of the pink family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Look at naughty ladies, getting shock

parts.note: to scan something is to look at it closely

indicators.note: naughty implies misbehaving, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: Ogling misbehaving women and causing outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage people's sense of propriety is to shock them, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One's beginning to paint, respecting such a technique

parts.note: one's means one is, I'm

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of paint

parts.note: as to means regarding or respecting

explanation.surface: A first step in painting with regard to a certain method.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying paint thickly so brush or knife marks stay visible is a painting technique, the one the clue describes.

indicators.note: the letter for are goes in the other pieces

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Waterfowl are found in an abandoned lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is the British endearment 'ducks', like 'love', not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England, ducks is an affectionate form of address, just like the answer, meaning darling.

indicators.note: badly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram
taken as written into the anagram
taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A movie turned out poorly, followed by an exclamation of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning as it should be, proper by social convention, hence correct.

clue.text: Function (police social) raised slightly less than half

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read from bottom to top
five of the twelve letters of police social, taken from the middle, are just under half of them

explanation.surface: A police party where a bit under half the attendees got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party but is a trigonometric function.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosecant, the reciprocal of sine, is a trigonometric function; this is its abbreviation.

indicators.note: baseless in a down clue drops the bottom letter of the word

parts.note: ardent means burning, passionate

explanation.surface: Is a woodland ablaze? That rumour lacks foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden in Warwickshire is the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It, a woodland.

indicators.note: stops as in plugs a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: An author named Oscar halts the workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer Oscar' suggests Wilde, but Oscar is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of tales and poems, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Anger that king has broken a bone

indicators.note: the king has broken into the phrase for anger, sitting inside it

parts.note: to stir up is to provoke or anger
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Fury that a monarch has fractured something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken a bone' reads as an injury; 'a bone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, a tiny bone in the middle ear, is commonly named after the saddle footrest it resembles.

clue.text: Old man with sweetheart in spot — reportedly a very low point

indicators.note: the sweetheart is in the word for old man

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for spot is swapped for its sound-alike

parts.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A father and his girlfriend in a place, described as a very low point in someone's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is the middle letter of SWEET, not a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan has the lowest land surface on Earth, literally a very low point.

clue.text: Can scoff but it saves time in the kitchen

definitions.text: it saves time in the kitchen

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, and a public convenience is one
scoff is British slang for food

explanation.surface: A claim that you may gobble something that makes cooking quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as 'may' but means a lavatory, as does a public CONVENIENCE in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready meals need little preparation, so their whole purpose is to cut cooking time.
